pass_a_gloss: And further Heracleon toward the “He says to her” says: clear that saying some such thing, if you want to receive this water, go call your husband. He thinks the husband said by the Savior of the Samaritan woman is her pleroma, in order that having come to be with that one toward the Savior she may be able to fetch the power and the union and the blending toward the pleroma. And concerning a worldly husband, he says, he was speaking to her that she might call, since indeed he was not ignorant that he whom she has is not her lawful husband. And clearly here he forces the text, saying the Savior has said “Call your husband and come here” making clear the consort from the pleroma. For if this held thus, it was necessary also to say in what manner he will have to be called, in order that she may come to be with him toward the Savior. But since, as Heracleon says, according to the understood sense she was ignorant of her own husband, but according to the simple sense she was ashamed to say that she had an adulterer and not a husband, how is it not vainly that the Savior was saying to her, “Call your husband”?
pass_b_english: Heracleon also takes [[“He says to her” >> Bible:John 4:16]] this way: Jesus means, in effect, “If you want this water, go call your husband.” Heracleon thinks the “husband” the Savior names is the Samaritan woman’s pleroma, so that once she comes with that consort to the Savior she may receive power, union, and blending with the pleroma.

As for a worldly husband, Heracleon says, Jesus told her to call one because he knew the man she had was not her lawful husband. But that reading plainly forces the text. If [[“Call your husband and come here” >> Bible:John 4:16]] meant the consort from the pleroma, Jesus would also have had to say how she was to call him so that she might come with him to the Savior.

Heracleon himself says that in the deeper sense she did not know her own husband, while in the plain sense she was ashamed to admit she had an adulterer rather than a husband. How, then, is it not empty for the Savior to tell her, “Call your husband”?
